summary.headline: Gallantt Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR 203 crore (18% margin) from INR 254 crore a year ago, though flat sequentially, on coal costs and a pellet plant shutdown.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 2% year-on-year to INR 1,146 crore but fell from INR 1,205 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA was INR 203 crore (18% margin) versus INR 209 crore in Q4 and INR 254 crore in Q1 FY26, and PAT was INR 124 crore (11% margin). Management attributed the year-on-year decline to higher raw material costs (up 9%), the planned pellet plant shutdown, a seasonal monsoon-driven TMT price correction, and higher employee costs. The 1.23 million tonne capacity expansion and captive iron ore mines remain on schedule for H2 FY27 and FY28 respectively.

segments.name: TMT / long products (Gorakhpur and Gujarat)
segments.commentary: TMT sales volume was flat YoY at about 192,000 tonnes and down about 8% QoQ against a strong Q4 FY26. Gorakhpur rolling mill utilisation is 93%, while Kutch is at about 66%.

segments.name: Pellet and sponge iron
segments.commentary: External sales fell YoY and QoQ due to higher captive consumption for DRI and steelmaking, plus the planned pellet plant shutdown, which is now complete.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: Billet volumes grew 13% YoY and 38% QoQ, running ahead of internal plans for the year.

guidance_outlook: Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes (0.23 million tonnes) under the INR 3,000 crore capex programme is expected to commission in H2 FY27, with benefits flowing from H2.
Pellet plant returns to normal captive utilisation in the coming quarter now the shutdown is complete; management expects no substantial EBITDA erosion through the year.
Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted because of the monsoon; management expects Q3 and Q4 to pick up.
Domestic steel demand expected to grow 7-9% this year; management referred to 8-9% in the Q&A.
Captive iron ore mines (UP and Rajasthan) are targeted to commence production in FY28; UP exploration expected to finish in 2-3 months and Rajasthan in about six months.
Solar: 18 MW in Gujarat due for Q2 FY27 and 60 MW at Gorakhpur due for Q4 FY27 (the call also cites 67 MW elsewhere, so the split is unclear).
Debottlenecking at Gujarat unit to complete within FY27.
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about INR 3,000 crore, of which about INR 800 crore spent over FY26 and Q1 FY27; INR 137 crore spent in Q1 FY27. Funded by internal accruals with no term loans planned.
Roughly half of capex goes to mining: three iron ore mines (two in UP, one in Rajasthan), with beneficiation plants in UP and a beneficiation-cum-pellet plant in Rajasthan. Production from FY28.
Capacity expansion from 1 million to 1.23 million tonnes, commissioning in H2 FY27.
Solar: 7 MW trial plant commissioned in FY26; 18 MW in Gujarat (Q2 FY27); 60 MW at Gorakhpur (Q4 FY27). Total about 85 MW.
Pellet plant installed capacity about 8 lakh tonnes against raw feed need of 9-9.5 lakh tonnes a year.
demand_pricing: TMT and rebar prices corrected meaningfully during the quarter from a firm start; management said the correction was seasonal and sector-wide, with flat products holding up better.
India turned a net steel importer in the quarter, with imports rising under some free trade routes; the industry has sought anti-dumping duties alongside existing safeguard duties.
Management claims a market share above 25% in its addressable UP market and cites brand marketing with celebrity endorsements (Ajay Devgn, and now Janhvi Kapoor).
Export: management said exports are not a focus. Gorakhpur is inland, and Gujarat billet exports happen only occasionally.

Raw material mix: Gorakhpur coal is 100% linkage for power plant; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian and the rest South African, sourced via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal for power and South African coal for process.

qa_highlights.question: What is the iron ore and pellet sourcing strategy, and who are the top suppliers?
qa_highlights.answer: Gorakhpur sources iron ore fines from Odisha Mineral Corporation, multiple Madhya Pradesh concentrate suppliers and Lloyds (Maharashtra), mixed on price and quality. Gorakhpur coal for power is 100% Indian linkage coal; DRI coal is 60-70% Indian with the rest South African via Itochu. Gujarat uses Indonesian coal via Mundra/Kandla for power and South African coal for process.

qa_highlights.question: Does high-phosphorus iron ore from Lloyds pose a problem?
qa_highlights.answer: Lloyds supplies only low-phosphorus material, about 15-20% of the mix, roughly 15,000 tonnes a month. Pellet plant capacity is about 8 lakh tonnes against 9-9.5 lakh tonnes of raw feed a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and funding, and how will UP market share and adjacent expansion be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR 3,000 crore, with about INR 800 crore spent so far; half goes to mining, with 85 MW solar and the 0.23 million tonne capacity addition in H2 FY27. All funded by internal accruals with no term loans. Management claims over 25% share of the addressable UP market and uses celebrity branding (Ajay Devgn, now Janhvi Kapoor), with other markets to follow as capacity grows.

qa_highlights.question: Are exports a realistic avenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a focus. Construction steel is logistically hard to export and Gorakhpur is inland; Gujarat billets are exported only occasionally.

qa_highlights.question: What drives margins and are they sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins have stayed around 17-18% across FY26 quarters, driven by pellet-to-TMT integration and no term debt. Management says margins are sustainable, with solar and FY28 captive mines expected to improve them.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat-product import pressure affecting long products, and what is the demand outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Flat-product price pressure spills over to long products to some extent. Management expects 8-9% steel demand growth, sees Q1 and Q2 as muted by monsoon, and expects pick-up from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are the captive iron ore mine timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Exploration in UP is expected to finish in 2-3 months and in Rajasthan in about six months. Management reiterated that all three mines should commission in FY28, not FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact and outlook on iron ore and coal?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs rose 9% YoY, about half of which relates to the pellet plant shutdown; 4-5% is price-driven across iron ore and coal. Coal is the main driver, with iron ore impacted mainly by sea freight; management sees no substantial EBITDA erosion for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA per tonne fall, and is it one-off or structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with the historical 17-18% range. FY26 EBITDA per tonne was about INR 8,800 and it is about INR 8,700 now, so the decline is attributed to pressure rather than structural change.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FY26 revenue growth slow, and will volumes return to double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the YoY revenue decline as marginal, about 2-2.5%. It expects volumes to be much higher once the H2 FY27 capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Coal and freight cost inflation (Middle East conflict, fuel prices) could keep raw material costs elevated; watch whether the 4-5% price-driven increase reverses.
Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted by monsoon; Kutch rolling mill utilisation at about 66% versus Gorakhpur at 93% needs to improve.
Execution risk on the 1.23 million tonne expansion (H2 FY27), 60 MW Gorakhpur solar (Q4 FY27) and captive mines (FY28), with UP and Rajasthan exploration and forest/environment clearances pending.
Cheap steel imports and flat-product price pressure could spill into TMT pricing; watch the anti-dumping decision.
Cash balance fell QoQ alongside higher receivables and inventory; management expects normalisation as collections pick up.
Management said it will evaluate debt or equity for the medium-term growth plan, to be shared next quarter; this could change the no-debt stance.
key_quotes: What we do take comfort from is that quarter-on-quarter our operating performance held its ground, which speaks to the resilience of our integrated model even through a seasonally and cyclically difficult quarter for the industry.
And definitely it is sustainable. We have a little bit of dent because of the geopolitical situation but despite that in the last quarter we have been able to maintain our EBITDA percentages.
So, while those targets are aggressive, considering the government regulatory involvement in the mining sector, currently we are on track to make it operational in FY28.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term demand and expansion timelines, but defensive on the year-on-year margin and profit decline, which it attributes to the pellet shutdown, coal costs and seasonality. Answers on the market and demand outlook were broadly reassuring; several answers were vague on specifics such as the Solar split (18 MW versus 67 MW) and mine timelines.
